attributes.body:
One of the common uses of the particle か is often translated to 'or' in English. While this translation is accurate, it is not actually any different from か's regular usage as a question marker.

From these examples, we can see that, in Japanese, か is performing the same role that a question mark would, or that a change in tone of voice would in spoken language.

'Would you like tea? coffee?' (said with a rising tone).

This nuance of か can be used after the dictionary form of almost any word in Japanese. However, using です or ます will change the nuance from 'presenting possibilities', to 'asking a formal question', so should be avoided.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.body: The particle か can follow nouns to mean 'or,' clearly specifying alternatives (e.g., 今日か明日休みます = 'I'll take off today or tomorrow'). On the other hand, でも, which also follows nouns, means 'or something,' suggesting an open-ended alternative (e.g., お茶でも飲みましょうか = 'Shall we drink tea or something?').

second_relatable.title: でも
second_relatable.meaning: Or something,  Any... (with question words), No matter (who)

attributes.body: Both か and それとも present alternatives. か directly follows nouns to mean 'or' (e.g., 今日か明日休みます = 'I'll take off today or tomorrow'). In contrast, それとも means 'or' as well, but is used at the start of sentences or questions, not directly after nouns (e.g., 今日休む？それとも明日にする？ = 'Will you take off today? Or [will you do it] tomorrow?').

Both か and あるいは present alternatives. か is casual and follows nouns to mean 'or' (e.g., 今日か明日休みます = 'I'll take off today or tomorrow'). あるいは is more formal, mainly used in writing or formal speech (e.g., 新品で買うか、あるいは中古で買うか、まだ決めていません = 'I haven't decided yet whether I'll buy it new or perhaps second-hand').

second_relatable.title: あるいは
second_relatable.meaning: Or, Possibly, Maybe, Perhaps, Or possibly

attributes.body: ～なり～なり is a somewhat formal or literary expression used to provide examples, typically implying additional options or suggesting that the speaker doesn't mind which option is chosen. In contrast, the question particle か is used after nouns to present alternatives or offer a choice between two or more items (e.g., 今日か明日休みます = 'I'll take off today or tomorrow').

Both uses of か are extensions of its basic function as a question particle. When following a Wh-question word (like who, what, where, why, how), it creates a phrase meaning 'some-(word)' (e.g., 誰か = 'someone,' どこか = 'somewhere,' いつか = 'sometime'). When following regular nouns, it means 'or' (e.g., 今日か明日休みます = 'I'll take off today or tomorrow').
